topic: Covert consciousness after severe brain injury
challenge: Does the absence of observable behavior AND a negative task-based EEG/fMRI command-following response establish absence of subjective awareness? What evidence would most help discriminate the remaining possibilities?

limitations: Modality and available assessments vary across people.
Observable response is not a perfect ground truth for all subjective experiences.
A task-based signal tests a demanding cognitive ability, not all forms of experience.
Aggregate heterogeneous methods and patient states.
Does not provide independent definitive subjective-experience ground truth.

source_cards.review_summary: Negative active command-following cannot exclude awareness; performance requires auditory/language/attention and task execution.
False negatives arise even in healthy or behaviorally command-following people; technical and fluctuating arousal confounds.

methodological_gaps: No ground-truth labels for all subjective experiences.
No externally validated sensitivity/specificity for the latent target SUBJECTIVE_EXPERIENCE_UNOBSERVED in this evidence packet.
No directly evidenced individual patient prior probability for the latent target.
No independent source authentication: human-curated URLs and counts only.
